newsitem.title: USA: Jackson suggests boycotts to fight TV sex, violence.
newsitem.headline: Jackson suggests boycotts to fight TV sex, violence.

text.p: Civil rights leader Rev. Jesse Jackson on Friday suggested that boycotts would be an effective way of changing the content of controversial television programmes that he said were "rotting our culture."

In an interview taped for Saturday's "Evans & Novak" programme on CNN, Jackson said censorship was not a viable option for getting rid of questionable programmes, but that boycotts could be an effective tool for parents.

"If there would be a selected ... boycott, it would get the attention of the competition," he said. "Right now, they feel no constraint but to dump onto the public, sex without love, and violence, and drugs... moral cultural lifestyles that are hurting the children and rotting our culture."
Jackson said such boycotts should be based on research "which documents (the) offensiveness" of television programmes, targeting advertisers and producers.
This strategy could be effective, given the extremely competitive nature of the television industry, Jackson said.
The television industry has just drafted a new system of ratings to be used with a new V-chip to allow parents to keep their children from watching programmes they deem unsuitable.
